title: Who is there to tell?
odia: କାହାକୁ କହିବା, କପାଳରେ ସିନା କର ମାରିବା
literal_meaning: Whom can one tell? One can only strike a hand against one’s forehead.
explanation: This is a gesture of exasperation put into words. The speaker feels that complaining will find no useful listener, so frustration turns into a weary reaction. It may be rueful or comic; it expresses a feeling of helplessness without proving that help is unavailable.
meaning_odia: କଥା ଶୁଣିବାକୁ କେହି ନାହାନ୍ତି ବୋଲି ବକ୍ତାଙ୍କୁ ଲାଗୁଛି; ବିରକ୍ତିରେ ନିଜ ମୁଣ୍ଡକୁ ହାତ ଯାଉଛି। ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରିବାର ଠିକଣା ନମିଳିବାର ଅସହାୟତାକୁ ଏହି ଅତିଶୟୋକ୍ତି ଧରେ। ଏହା ମୁହୂର୍ତ୍ତର କ୍ଷୋଭ, ସତରେ ସାହାଯ୍ୟର ସବୁ ବାଟ ବନ୍ଦ ବୋଲି ନିଷ୍କର୍ଷ ନୁହେଁ।
usage_example: After correcting the same simple mistake several times, a person says this with a tired laugh. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: କର means hand here. The literal gesture helps convey the expression; no physical action is prescribed by the explanation.

english_summary: A weary complaint expresses the feeling that there is nobody useful to tell.
